summary: An unchanged RAW Apply re-developed the image and discarded the current picture and Denoise preparation.
evidence: M1-15. Paired HDR Fit GPU audit on MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 8 GB, 1408x794, AC), Sony _DSC7970.ARW (42.39 MP), three measured clicks and one warmup per action. The same Apply with preflight forced to decline had a 5572.2 ms median whole wait (5056.1–5819.7 ms). Reuse measured 328.5 ms (325.7–336.5 ms) with no import job or new frame and the identical compositor signature. Lens on/off still changed pixels. Both changed-control rows took the full development route and all 14 rows completed without errors.
felt_impact: Unchanged Apply saved 5.24 s at the median on the 42 MP Sony, a 94% reduction. Changed RAW controls still do the full work.
proposed_fix: Before releasing the GPU, have the backend verify the current session/revision, source stat and SHA-256, accepted editable recipe, and applicable Lensfun database identity. Ignore resolved Auto provenance when comparing controls, but require the normal path to save the same recipe. Keep the existing dirty/revision/recovery and success status effects.
check: 116 targeted Node tests, 67 targeted Python tests and the locked raw.lens audit passed. Run the raw.lens Fit HDR audit with HDR_FINISHER_AUDIT_RAW_APPLY_BASELINE=1 to add the forced-normal comparator. Local evidence: codebase/output/audits/O3/module-impact-typical-fit.json.
notes: The measured preflight reopened and serialized the Lensfun database. Before commit this was tightened to verify the bundled XML bytes and refuse reuse if system/user profiles can contribute, avoiding the serialization cost. The final guard passed the targeted tests, but the 328.5 ms app timing is from the earlier preflight. Lens Off does not consult Lensfun. The other O3 checkpoint/cache items were not changed.
